parts.title: Socotra Island
parts.article:
(A) When scientists began the first substantial exploration of the islands 30 years ago, they found a fascinating collection of unusual plants and animals - a unique combination of 'relict' populations (organisms that have become extinct elsewhere) and species that have evolved to cope with the island's harsh conditions. In fact, almost a third of its plant species and up to 80 percent of its terrestrial animals are found nowhere else.

(B) Life in the arid conditions is harsh for the people living there too. Isolated from the mainland by hundreds of kilometres, and with monsoons that rage for several months every year, the islanders were historically self-sufficient - relying only on what they themselves could produce to survive. There are floods and droughts, and many islanders lack adequate water resources and nutrition. Medical care and education are limited.

(C) However, the main island, Socotra, is experiencing significant change. A rapid development programme has been instituted that will have far-reaching impacts on the island's people and the environment for decades to come. In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat, but irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s. By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra that was capable of taking larger aircraft all year round, and since 2000 the capital, Hadibo, has seen huge expansion. New schools have been built, and a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass. And there are plans to construct new harbour facilities that will enable fishermen to sell their catch more easily, and also make it simpler for local people to have food, and bricks and timber for construction projects brought to the island.

(D) However, although these improvements are significant, it’s the continuing development of Socotra’s road system that is having the greatest impact on the islanders. Until 1991, a few dirt tracks, navigable only by four-wheel drive, gave access to part of the island. Otherwise it was only possible to reach most areas on foot, or with a donkey. By 2001, however, there was an extensive network of unpaved car tracks, and the following year a tarmac road, the first of its kind on Socotra, connecting the airport to Hadibo, was completed. Now, a road traverses the Diksam plateau and continues on to the south coast, making essential services more accessible to a large number of villagers.

(E) There is no doubt that the development of Socotra’s infrastructure has brought many benefits to the island's inhabitants, but there is growing concern that the speed with which it is taking place is so rapid that it will be difficult for local people to maintain certain traditions. There is also the fear that the developments will threaten the island's unique ecosystems. Building new roads and harbours may lead to the introduction of alien species to Socotra Island (as has already happened with the Indian house crow), damage to the sea's biodiversity through the increased collection and sale of coral, and tourist developments on an inappropriate and unsustainable scale.

(F) Problems were also caused by increasing access to sensitive areas. For example, cutting the road along the coast caused considerable damage to the stunning scenery. However, some steps were then taken to limit the damage caused by further development. For example, biodiversity project officers were consulted in the planning stages of the road that crosses the centre of Socotra, so it avoids some of the most scenic areas and sites that contain plants only found in a limited number of locations. It is an area which is also home to the greatest concentrations of dragon's blood trees and supports many endemic animals.

(G) An agreement has now been reached about all future construction of roads. To protect the island's ecologically sensitive areas, any proposed road will be subject to a report assessing its environmental impact prior to construction. The challenge has been to bring the benefits of development to Socotra without damaging the environment, which supports the people's way of life and will form the basis of future development on the island.

reference:
Q1

解析 原文明确提到科学家发现了在其他地方已经灭绝（become extinct elsewhere）的生物，也就是题目说的“在其他国家已经死绝的物种”。

干扰 你可能会因为没认出extinct（灭绝）和died out的同义替换而不敢选TRUE。

句子 When scientists began the first substantial exploration of the islands 30 years ago, they found a fascinating collection of unusual plants and animals - a unique combination of 'relict' populations (organisms that have become extinct elsewhere) and species that have evolved to cope with the island's harsh conditions.

Q2

解析 原文说岛民在历史上是“自给自足的（self-sufficient）”，这直接反驳了题目所说的“依赖大陆（dependent on the mainland）”。

句子 Isolated from the mainland by hundreds of kilometres, and with monsoons that rage for several months every year, the islanders were historically self-sufficient - relying only on what they themselves could produce to survive.

Q3

解析 原文确实提到了最早的航班是“不规律的（irregular）”，但根本没有提到是因为“糟糕的天气情况（poor weather conditions）”导致的。

干扰 你可能会自己脑补前面段落提到的季风（monsoons）影响了航班，但这两句话之间并没有建立因果关系，做题时千万不要自行加戏。

句子 In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat, but irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s.

Q4

解析 原文只提到了首都经历了大规模扩张，以及越来越多游客通过机场，但完全没提游客是否“大多数都住在首都”。

句子 By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra that was capable of taking larger aircraft all year round, and since 2000 the capital, Hadibo, has seen huge expansion. New schools have been built, and a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass.

Q5

解析 原文明确指出，对岛民影响最大的（greatest impact）是道路系统（road system）的持续发展，直接反驳了题目说的机场（airport）影响最大。

干扰 你可能只看到了上一段大篇幅关于机场的建设，但没看到这一段开头的转折句明确把“最深刻的影响”归给了道路。

句子 However, although these improvements are significant, it’s the continuing development of Socotra’s road system that is having the greatest impact on the islanders.

Q6

解析 题目问过去只能通过什么到达岛屿，原文直接对应“唯一的途径是坐几天船（by travelling for several days on a boat）”。

句子 In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat, but irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s.

Q7

解析 题目问机场跑道是哪一年建成的，原文直接给出了时间点“到1999年，跑道已经建成（had been constructed）”。

句子 By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra that was capable of taking larger aircraft all year round, and since 2000 the capital, Hadibo, has seen huge expansion.

Q8

解析 题目问机场用最新的什么进行了扩建，原文指出机场增加了一个现代化的航站楼（modern terminal），其中modern完美替换了题目的up-to-date。

句子 New schools have been built, and a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass.

Q9

解析 题目问港口让进口什么东西和建筑材料变得更容易，原文提到运到岛上的有食物（food）、砖块和木材（建筑材料）。

干扰 你可能会填错成bricks或者timber，但这两个词已经被题目里的“building materials”概括合并了，所以剩下的并列项只有food。

句子 And there are plans to construct new harbour facilities that will enable fishermen to sell their catch more easily, and also make it simpler for local people to have food, and bricks and timber for construction projects brought to the island.

Q10

解析 题目列举了新公路建成前进入岛屿的交通方式：步行、四驱车或者什么，原文准确对应了步行（on foot）、驴（donkey）和四驱车（four-wheel drive）。

句子 Until 1991, a few dirt tracks, navigable only by four-wheel drive, gave access to part of the island. Otherwise it was only possible to reach most areas on foot, or with a donkey.

Q11

解析 题目问因为发展速度太快，当地居民将更少保留什么，原文直接说当地人将很难维持某些传统（maintain certain traditions）。

句子 There is no doubt that the development of Socotra’s infrastructure has brought many benefits to the island's inhabitants, but there is growing concern that the speed with which it is taking place is so rapid that it will be difficult for local people to maintain certain traditions.

Q12

解析 题目问官员确保新道路没有穿过含有稀有什么的地点，原文说避开了包含“只在极少数地方发现的植物（plants only found in a limited number of locations）”的区域。

干扰 你可能会想填animals，但原文说到特有动物（endemic animals）是在后面单独的一句，而与避开的具体区域紧密相连的是植物（plants）。

句子 For example, biodiversity project officers were consulted in the planning stages of the road that crosses the centre of Socotra, so it avoids some of the most scenic areas and sites that contain plants only found in a limited number of locations.

Q13

解析 题目问未来道路建设造成的环境破坏将在什么文件中进行评估，原文明确说明任何拟建道路在施工前都要出具一份评估环境影响的报告（report）。

句子 To protect the island's ecologically sensitive areas, any proposed road will be subject to a report assessing its environmental impact prior to construction.
